done: Landed the CAP-DOCS-01 authored-snippet safeguard in scripts/docs-data/authored-snippets.ts (inventory of every code-bearing block in apps/docs/src/content/docs — fenced blocks plus MDX readFileSync exports feeding CodeBlock props, 8 displayed blocks / 6 identities over 7 documents; committed provenance bindings pinning whole files or sha256+byte-length regions that must match exactly one window; byte comparison of authored and emitted bytes; required configuration inputs for both engine packages; consumer assembly via the committed public recipe with real tsc --noEmit per cloned case and the live-chat tsconfig.live-chat.json import-graph compiler; optional --check-emitted drift rejection), apps/docs/src/components/SourceSnippet.astro (source-addressed display with byte-exact copy over the unmodified rnr-copy-button island and provenance attributes), tests/sprint-05-orient-search/authored-snippet-gate.test.ts (all four ACs proven against real filesystem copies, real tsc processes, a real Astro build + owned preview server, and real Chromium clipboard), and tests/sprint-05-orient-search/evidence/ORI-AST-005/manifest.json plus .tmp/ORI-AST-005/cycle-1/{red,green} evidence; RED was observed on all four selectors before GREEN (4 pass / 0 fail on the final bytes; gate, typecheck, biome, and fallow all exit 0).
deviations: Committed provenance lives as a bindings table inside scripts/docs-data/authored-snippets.ts (COMMITTED_BINDINGS) instead of in-document annotations, because apps/docs/src/content/** is write-prohibited; a --bindings flag extends/replaces the table for owned scratch proof pages and the unbinding negative cases.

Named-region bindings pin the selection by sha256 + BYTE length resolved as a unique window in the source (duplicate windows fail as ambiguous), so region identity is byte-based — the test side must use Buffer.byteLength, not JS string length, on the seed text's multibyte em dashes.

Owner-compiler contexts are assembled rather than assumed: packages/docs-snippets/<engine> as committed has no installed deps and no shared/, so the gate runs the committed recipe verbatim in an owned cache keyed by dependency identity, clones it per compile case, syncs the CURRENT corpus sources into the clone, and compiles there so mutations are what the real compiler sees.

The AC-3 proof page is created inside an owned repo-shaped scratch docs copy (root package.json, scripts/docs-data, packages/docs-snippets symlink, node_modules links) because no page may import the dark-work SourceSnippet inside this task's write scope.

Fallow compliance reshaped two spots: kindFromFenceLang became a lookup table, and the byte-fidelity body moved into a named byteFidelityProof() helper; the remaining gate drivers take the house fallow-ignore-next-line complexity suppression, and the CLI entry is de-exported after fallow flagged the unused export.
Compiler receipts record executable/config at their persistent cache paths because the per-case clone (the receipt's cwd) is removed on every exit path.
concerns: The consumer cache under <tmpdir>/ori-ast-005-consumers (plus --consumer-cache) persists by design and is a shared mutable surface: AC-4's dependency-removal case deletes node_modules/react-native from the nativewind cache and restores it via pnpm install, so two lanes running the gate concurrently on one machine can interleave badly (within the serial task suite this is safe).

A cold machine pays two full consumer assemblies (~25s each warm store, minutes cold, plus network to npm, Expo, and rnraielements.com) before any compiler receipt exists; CI wiring should expect that on first run.

apps/docs/src/components/SourceSnippet.astro:2 carries a load-bearing fallow-ignore-file unused-file directive — nothing may wire the component into a page until a later task either adds a page (and removes the directive) or the corpus task owns it.

The emission check extracts rendered bytes by entity-decoding the built HTML (named plus numeric entities); a future Astro text-escaping change would surface as pristine-check byte mismatches rather than silent passes, but it is a coupling to Astro's escaping behavior.
Region resolution is an O(n×m) sliding sha256 scan — fine for KB-scale sources, a ceiling if a future binding targets a multi-megabyte file.
findings: The authored corpus holds exactly 6 code identities displayed as 8 blocks — quickstart.mdx renders messagesSource and screenSource once per engine tab, so bindings are matched per identity and not consumed per instance.

Both authored fences' provenance claims are byte-true: cli.md:19 is a unique 105-byte window of packages/docs-snippets/commands/nativewind.sh, and theming.mdx:25-33 is a unique 838-byte window of apps/example/global.css.

packages/docs-snippets/<engine> packages are consumer templates — no shared/, no node_modules, and '@/shared/quickstart-screen' resolves only after assembly — but the committed recipe runs verbatim in ~22s with a warm pnpm store including its own tsc and expo-doctor steps.

Astro 7's JSX-mode compressHTML does not trim {expr} code text: served <code> textContent stayed byte-exact to the prop including terminal newlines, extending the AST-001/CONT-003 finding to SourceSnippet.

A bare .astro page without <meta charset> mojibakes non-ASCII code text in the browser (em dashes rendered as â€”), so any future bare-layout proof page must declare charset or rendered-byte comparisons fail.

Fallow's suppression directive parses every whitespace-separated token on the line as an issue kind — trailing prose after '// fallow-ignore-file unused-file' spawns one stale-suppression finding per word.

Scratch docs builds need four repo-shape elements beyond the app copy: root package.json (src/pages/index.astro), scripts/docs-data (TokenTable.astro's token-map import), a root node_modules symlink (qrcode from pages/components/[item].astro), and a packages/docs-snippets symlink (quickstart.mdx's build-time readFileSync).

apps/example/tsconfig.live-chat.json plus apps/example's own tsc is the ready-made live-example import-graph compiler the VP-EXAMPLE-DIAGNOSTICS precondition refers to, and it compiles clean at TypeScript 6.0.3.

scope_impact.found: The check:snippets stage command is `pnpm exec tsx scripts/docs-data/authored-snippets.ts` (exit 0 = pass; diagnostics on stderr; JSON report on stdout) and it owns a persistent consumer cache under --consumer-cache (default <tmpdir>/ori-ast-005-consumers) that must not be wiped between stages.
scope_impact.change: Wire that exact command into the ordered public build; budget the first cold run for two consumer assemblies (~25s each warm store, minutes cold with npm/Expo/registry network), and do not place it before prebuild in a way that assumes no network.

scope_impact.found: Every future task that adds an authored code block (any content or docs task touching apps/docs/src/content/docs) must add the matching entry to COMMITTED_BINDINGS in scripts/docs-data/authored-snippets.ts in the same change.
scope_impact.change: State in the content-task template that new authored code blocks land together with their binding (source path, and region sha256+byte-length for regions) or the snippet gate will fail closed with an unbound-block diagnostic; that failure is the design, not a bug.

scope_impact.found: AC-1's five-kind coverage clause is observed as TS/TSX/shell/CSS from the 8 real authored blocks plus configuration via the 16 committed engine-package configuration inputs; the authored corpus contains no configuration-language block and apps/docs/src/content is write-prohibited, so the kind could not be authored here.
scope_impact.change: If the planner wants a configuration-language authored block provenance-pinned (e.g. a tailwind.config.js or metro.config.js fence on theming or a setup page), it needs a content task whose write scope covers apps/docs/src/content; the gate will then require and verify its binding automatically.

feedback: Dark-work component charters should pre-authorize the fallow suppression (or a config alwaysUsed entry) for the unwired deliverable — discovering fallow's directive token semantics (every word on the line must be an issue kind) cost several audit iterations.

Charters that enumerate required content kinds should cross-check the landed corpus first: the 'configuration' kind was written before ORI-CONT-001/003 landed, and nothing the dependencies produced ever displayed a configuration file.

In this harness TMPDIR resolves to ~/.cache/agent-scratch, so leaked preview servers and scratch copies are best hunted by lsof cwd and agent-scratch paths, not /tmp heuristics; rtk also truncates vitest output, so capture suite verdicts by appending explicit exit markers inside the same shell.
